paper.title_en: Partition of initial angular momentum in nuclear fission
paper.abstract_en: This article reports the first measurement of the total prompt <math><mi>γ</mi></math>-ray multiplicity in fast-neutron-induced fission of uranium-238 up to 30 MeV. The observed increase with neutron energy directly constrains angular momentum transfer. Combining high-efficiency <math><mi>γ</mi></math>-ray measurements with fully microscopic time-dependent Hartree-Fock calculations including pairing, we show that only about 30% of the additional angular momentum is carried by the fragments, while 70% remains as orbital motion. A scenario of full transfer to fragment spins is incompatible with the data. The results instead support a picture where fragment spins are partially aligned, reflecting the interplay between dynamical angular momentum transfer and quantum fluctuations. These findings support the interpretation that orbital motion constitutes the dominant angular momentum reservoir in fission.
